title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): Grothendieck is axiomatising 'ateliers' for a combinatorial analysis situs. There are two base sets: M ('multistates', to be read as elementary cells or pieces) and F ('figures', to be read as subcomplexes). They are linked by an incidence relation X ◁ F. For F in F, F̃ = {X | X ◁ F}. AtM1 says F ↦ F̃ is injective and F̃ separates the points of M. AtM2 says each X has a least figure F_X containing it. AtM3 says (a) a family of members of F̃ that is bounded by a member of F̃ has its union in F̃, and (b) F is nonempty.

This page:
(1) Specialisation order. Define X ≤ Y iff F_X ≤ F_Y. Tautologically this holds iff every figure containing Y contains X, iff X ◁ F_Y, iff X ∈ F̃_Y. This is the specialisation preorder of the family of subsets F̃ of M, exactly as for an Alexandrov topology. By the separation axiom AtM1 b) it is a partial order. The margin note sets X̃ := F̃_X = M_{≤X}, the principal down-set of X.
(2) Proposition. If Φ ∈ F̃, every 'closed' subset Ψ ⊂ Φ (closed meaning a down-set for ≤) lies in F̃. Proof, implicit and correct: Ψ is the union of the X̃ for X in Ψ. Each X̃ is in F̃ and contained in Φ, so AtM3 a) applies. Conversely the Proposition plus AtM2 gives back AtM3 a), since a bounded union of down-sets is a down-subset of the bound. Grothendieck notes the Proposition is formally stronger and can replace AtM3 a) given the other axioms. He kept the weaker form because it is expressible purely in terms of (F, ≤), as an axiom of existence of sups of bounded families.
Resulting picture: F̃ is a downward-hereditary family of down-sets of the poset M that contains all principal down-sets. Equivalently, (F, ≤) is the poset of 'admissible' sub-down-sets, a bornology-like ideal of down-sets.
(3) Compatibility. F ≍ G iff {F, G} is bounded in F, iff the sup F∨G exists (by AtM3), iff F̃ ∪ G̃ ∈ F̃. For multistates, X ≍ Y iff F_X ≍ F_Y, i.e. X̃ ∪ Ỹ ∈ F̃.
- AtM4 (coherence): F ≍ G iff X ≍ Y for all X ∈ F̃ and Y ∈ G̃. So boundedness of a pair of figures is detected pointwise.
- AtM5 ties ≍ to the magazine relations ≪ and |o| on M (|o| presumably 'disjointness'). X ≍ Y iff every X' ∈ X̃ outside X̃∩Ỹ is |o|-disjoint from every Y' ∈ Ỹ outside X̃∩Ỹ.
Geometric meaning: two closed cells form a subcomplex together exactly when they meet only along common faces. This is the regular-CW / polyhedral-complex intersection condition.
The next page counts the axioms: from the M-side one needs only the magazine axioms Mag1–4 plus one axiom on the choice of F. It then passes to 'polyhedral' ateliers (prepolyideal magazines).
Overall purpose: show that the 'symmetric' presentation (M, F, ◁) is equivalent to a poset M with extra relations plus a choice of admissible down-sets, so that 'spaces' are encoded combinatorially.
errors: No mathematical error. The Proposition's proof is omitted but immediate (Ψ is a union of principal down-sets bounded by Φ, so AtM3 a) applies).
'Par AtM1 bis' in the transcription should be AtM1 b); antisymmetry of ≤ follows from point-separation, which makes X ↦ F_X injective.
AtM5 as transcribed (X', Y' both in X̃∩Ỹ) would make no sense, since elements of the common part need not be disjoint. The intended reading is surely X' ∈ X̃∖(X̃∩Ỹ), Y' ∈ Ỹ∖(X̃∩Ỹ).
AtM4 'F ≍ G ⟺ ∀X∈F̃, Y∈G̃, X≍Y': the ⇒ direction follows from the Proposition. Only ⇐ is a genuine axiom (pairwise coherence), and it is not automatic for infinite figures.

ideas.what: Order on multistates defined by X ≤ Y iff X lies in every figure containing Y, i.e. X ∈ F̃_Y; it is a partial order under the separation axiom
ideas.modern_name: specialisation preorder of a family of subsets / Alexandrov topology

ideas.what: The figures of an atelier are exactly a downward-hereditary family of down-sets of (M, ≤) containing the principal ones; 'bounded sups exist' is equivalent to this
ideas.modern_name: subcomplexes of a face poset / ideal of down-sets (bornology on a poset); bounded-complete poset of figures
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (face posets of regular CW complexes, Björner 1984; bounded-complete domains, Scott)

ideas.what: Compatibility relation ≍ (pair bounded / union is a figure), with axiom AtM4 that compatibility of figures is detected pointwise on their cells
ideas.modern_name: coherence / pairwise consistency (coherent domains, coherence spaces)

ideas.what: AtM5: two cells are compatible iff their parts outside the common faces are disjoint
ideas.modern_name: intersection axiom for regular CW / polyhedral complexes (cells meet in a union of common faces)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics of figures over multistates (bounded sups, plus pairwise-determined compatibility AtM4) is essentially a coherent bounded-complete domain / coherence-space structure, used here as a foundation for combinatorial tame topology. The domain-theory parallel was not drawn in either community.
missed.quote: AtM4 F ≍ G ⟺ ∀X ∈ F̃, Y ∈ G̃, on a X ≍ Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only mildly: it links Grothendieck's late 'analysis situs' program to domain theory and coherence spaces (contemporaneous, Girard 1987). The content itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but elementary order-theoretic reformulation of axioms in the unpublished 1986 'Analysis situs' project. The ideas (specialisation order, hereditary families of down-sets, pairwise coherence, the cells-meet-along-faces condition) are standard. Interest is mainly historical, as a glimpse of the axiomatics of 'ateliers/magazins'.

'Soit Φ ∈ F̃, alors ⇒ partie fermée Ψ/ de Φ' should be 'Soit Φ ∈ F̃, alors toute partie fermée Ψ de Φ est dans F̃'.

'{F, G} a un sup dans F ⟺ F ∪ G [?]' likely reads '{F, G} majoré dans F ⟺ F∨G existe' (sup exists).
